name: Lingon
description: Lingon helps you learn Swedish by reading real news from SVT, TV4, and Expressen. Three reading modes let you adjust as you go — full translations, side-by-side, or Swedish only.

features.title: Three Reading Modes
features.description: Read in Swedish only, with translations, or side-by-side. Swipe to switch anytime.

features.title: Built-in Dictionary
features.description: Long-press any word to look it up. No app-switching needed.

features.title: AI Simplification
features.description: Tap Simplify to rewrite any article in shorter sentences with everyday vocabulary.

features.title: Chat Tutor
features.description: Ask questions about grammar, vocabulary, or anything in the article you're reading.

features.title: Read Aloud
features.description: Hear articles spoken in Swedish. Pro users get five voice options and speed control.

features.title: On-Device Translation
features.description: Translations run on-device by default. Pro subscribers get cloud translations as a fallback.

faq.question: What language does Lingon teach?
faq.answer: Lingon is designed for learning Swedish. Articles come from SVT, TV4, and Expressen. Translations are available in English, Chinese, Arabic, French, and German.

faq.question: Do I need an internet connection?
faq.answer: You need internet to fetch news articles. Translations use Apple's on-device models when available, so they work without sending data to external servers.

faq.question: What devices are supported?
faq.answer: Lingon requires an iPhone running iOS 26.2 or later.

faq.question: What does the Pro subscription include?
faq.answer: Pro subscribers get unlimited articles, cloud translations via Gemini API as a fallback, unlimited AI chat messages, five Swedish TTS voices with speed control, and unlimited saved articles.

faq.question: How do I look up a word?
faq.answer: Long-press any word in an article to bring up the built-in iOS dictionary.

faq.question: How do I restore my subscription?
faq.answer: Open the app, go to Settings, tap Premium, then tap Restore Purchases at the bottom of the screen.

privacy:
Last updated: March 23, 2026

Lingon respects your privacy. This policy explains what data the app accesses and how it is handled.

Data Stored on Your Device
Your saved articles, reading preferences, and settings are stored locally on your device. No account or sign-in is required.

On-Device Translation
Translations are processed on-device using Apple Foundation Models whenever possible. No text is sent to external servers for standard translations.

News Content
The app fetches news articles from public RSS feeds (SVT, TV4, Expressen, 8 Sidor). Firebase is used to deliver pre-translated article data.

Pro Features & Third-Party Services
Pro subscribers may have article text sent to Google's Gemini API for cloud translation, AI simplification, and AI chat. Only the article text and your chat messages are sent — no personal information is included.

Subscriptions
Subscription purchases are handled entirely by Apple through StoreKit. Lingon does not process or store any payment information.

No Tracking or Advertising
Lingon does not include advertising, does not use tracking frameworks, and does not collect personal data.

Data Deletion
Deleting the app removes all locally stored data.

Contact
For privacy questions, contact chengdai.dev@gmail.com.

name: Search Switch
description: Use Brave, Startpage, Qwant or Mojeek from Safari’s address bar. Open Search Switch in Safari and pick an engine from the dropdown. Works on iPhone, iPad and Mac.

features.title: Four search engines
features.description: Choose Brave, Startpage, Qwant or Mojeek. Your choice saves automatically.

features.title: Easy to turn off
features.description: Choose Off to use Safari’s usual search engine again.

features.title: No account needed
features.description: Your choice stays on your device. The extension has no analytics or advertising.

faq.question: How do I set it up on iPhone or iPad?
faq.answer: Install Search Switch, then open Settings → Apps → Safari → Extensions → Search Switch and turn on Allow Extension. On older iOS versions, Safari is directly in Settings. In Safari, open the page menu or Extensions menu, choose Search Switch, and select an engine. Allow access to the search websites when Safari asks.

faq.question: How do I set it up on Mac?
faq.answer: Open Search Switch after installing it. In Safari → Settings → Extensions, enable Search Switch. Open it from Safari’s toolbar and choose an engine. Allow access to the search websites when Safari asks.

faq.question: Why does it need website access?
faq.answer: Safari needs permission for both the original search website and your chosen engine to apply a redirect. You can manage these permissions in Safari’s extension settings. Search Switch does not read result pages or keep a search history.

faq.question: Which searches can it redirect?
faq.answer: It redirects standard web searches on google.com, bing.com, duckduckgo.com, search.yahoo.com and ecosia.org, including searches started from Safari’s address bar. Searches made directly on these sites also redirect. Other regional domains and search formats may not work. Image, news and other search filters are not carried over.

faq.question: Why are searches still going to Safari’s usual engine?
faq.answer: Check that Search Switch is enabled, the dropdown is set to an engine rather than Off, and Safari has allowed access to both search websites. If you use Safari profiles, enable the extension for that profile too. Then try a new address-bar search. If your usual engine uses an unsupported regional domain, try DuckDuckGo in Safari’s Search settings.

faq.question: Does it change search suggestions?
faq.answer: No. Safari’s Search Engine Suggestions still come from the engine selected in Safari’s own Search settings. You can turn those suggestions off there. Search Switch redirects the search after you submit it.

faq.question: How do I turn it off?
faq.answer: Open Search Switch in Safari and choose Off. Safari will use its usual search engine again. You can also disable the extension in Safari’s settings.

faq.question: Does it work in Private Browsing?
faq.answer: Safari controls extension access in Private Browsing separately. Allow Search Switch in Private Browsing in Safari’s extension settings if you want to use it there.

privacy:
Last updated: October 19, 2026

Search Switch is a Safari extension made by Cheng Dai. This policy covers the app and extension on iPhone, iPad and Mac.

Data Stored on Your Device
Search Switch saves your selected search engine and whether redirection is on or off in the extension’s local storage. It does not send these settings to me or use its own sync service.

Searches and Search Providers
Safari applies redirect rules to supported search URLs and sends the query to your chosen provider: Brave, Startpage, Qwant or Mojeek. Safari’s usual search engine may also receive the query before redirection and when providing search suggestions. These providers handle queries, IP addresses and other connection data under their own privacy policies. Search Switch does not read the text on result pages or save a search history.

Website Permissions
Safari requires permission for both the original search website and the chosen provider for redirects to work. The extension declares access only to supported search websites. You control this access in Safari’s extension settings and can revoke it at any time.

No Accounts, Advertising or App Analytics
The app and extension have no accounts, advertising, analytics SDKs or developer-operated backend. They do not send searches, browsing history or usage analytics to me.

Retention and Deletion
Local settings are kept for as long as the extension’s local data remains on your device. Choosing Off stops redirection but keeps your saved engine choice. You can disable Search Switch or revoke its website access in Safari at any time. To remove its local settings, uninstall the extension and its containing app. Safari’s browsing history and records held by search providers are managed separately. I hold no server-side app settings or search records to delete.

Support Email
If you email me, I receive your email address and the information you include. I use this to reply and troubleshoot the issue, and keep the correspondence for as long as needed to handle your request. You can ask me to delete it by emailing chengdai.dev@gmail.com. Please avoid including private search queries or other sensitive information.

This Website
This support website is hosted on Vercel and uses Vercel Web Analytics for aggregate traffic statistics, including page views, referrers, browser, device and approximate location. It also loads fonts from Google Fonts. These website services receive connection data when you visit these pages; they are separate from the extension and do not receive search queries from Search Switch.

Changes to This Policy
If the app’s data handling changes, I will update this page and its date.

Contact
For questions about Search Switch or this policy, contact Cheng Dai at chengdai.dev@gmail.com.
